You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2017. The unemployment rate of 4.8% doesn't fit, though, since it was about 4.1% in late 2017. Some of the other readings do fit.

Fed funds at 0.66% with a 12m change of +0.37 suggests the rate was about 0.3% a year earlier. That points to early 2017, or possibly late 2016 (fed funds was about 0.41% in Dec 2016 and 0.66% in Mar 2017). Headline CPI at 2.54% YoY fits Jan or Feb 2017 (2.5% in Jan, 2.7% in Feb). The 10-year at 2.36% fits Feb 2017 (about 2.4%). The 2-year at 1.20% fits too. US equities returned +24.8% over 12 months, which is consistent with Feb 2017, as are a 3-month return of 7.4% and a 12m dollar change of +2%. The 20y+ Treasury drawdown of 14% matches the sell-off after the 2016 election.

Unemployment of 4.8% fits Jan 2017 (4.7-4.8%, depending on revision). Gold at +5.1% for the month fits Feb 2017. The 1-month equity return of +3.3% also fits Feb 2017 (S&P up 4%). The fed funds rate was 0.66% in Feb 2017 and 0.55% in Jan. Headline CPI for Jan was 2.5%, so I'll go with Jan or Feb 2017. VIX at 12.09 fits Feb 2017 (about 12.9 at month end). Core CPI at 2.26% fits Jan 2017 (2.3%). I'm choosing Feb 2017.
